**About DEUNA** \uD83E\uDDE1

We are a rapidly growing startup that simplifies global payments and powers next generation commerce in a single platform. With our products we've consolidated hundreds of payment solutions in a single integration, harness an intuitive payment orchestration method and centralize payment reconciliation.

We are currently present all across LATAM and looking for exceptional talent to join our team and continue revolutionizing the world of payments! \uD83D\uDE80

Visit https://www.deuna.com/ to learn more about us!

**About the Role**

We are looking for a hands-on data science leader to own machine learning and experimentation for DEUNA’s payments platform. You will be building the foundations of the data science practice at Deuna, working independently to design, train, and validate models that increase conversion, reduce declines, and reduce fraud in real-time payment flows across merchants and payment providers. You will be a part of the technology organization and will collaborate with project leads who own AI and modeling solutions for our customers, alongside existing data engineering and BI teams who already manage our data foundations and inference services. As DEUNA’s AI efforts grow, so will the team, and this role is a technical leadership role, with potential for people leadership if the skills align.

**Who You Are**

* You have 5+ years of experience applying machine learning to real production problems, ideally in payments, fintech, fraud, or other high-volume transactional environments.
* You think like a research scientist: you start from a problem, decide what data you need, choose the right modeling approach, and define how you will prove it works.
* You have hands-on depth in feature generation, model selection, training, and hyperparameter optimization, and you know when a simple model beats a complex one.
* You have designed and run experiments, including A/B testing and experimentation platforms, and can explain how you validated that a model delivered impact.
* You are proficient in Python and SQL and comfortable querying large datasets in tools like Snowflake. Familiarity with tools such as TensorFlow and Airflow is expected, and you can explain how you have managed and rolled out models.
* You are self-directed. You push for the information you need, and you do not need close supervision to keep work moving.
* You communicate clearly with technical and non-technical audiences, including setting realistic expectations with leadership about what models can and cannot achieve.
* You have experience in guiding technical infrastructure teams to implement features that enable efficient data science and ML training pipelines and systems

  

**What You’ll Do**

* Own the end-to-end modeling lifecycle for DEUNA’s payment optimization use cases: analyze merchant and transaction data, define modeling strategy, generate features, train and tune models, and release them through our existing inference infrastructure.
* Build the experimentation framework we need to measure model performance while collaborating with system and infra engineers, from early signals through month-over-month results, and tie that performance to commitments on our merchant contracts and product pipeline.
* Partner with data teams to define and track building of data processing pipelines that surface insights that shape what DEUNA delivers. You will use experiments and rapid model iteration to tailor approaches to merchant data and goals, and work with the existing models while building new ones.

**What will you find when you join DEUNA?**

* A multicultural team distributed throughout LATAM
* Dynamism, agility and constant innovation
* Being part of a high-impact solution for an entire region
* The best tools and technology to operate
* Being part of the startup culture.
* We are in full expansion!

Vacations and additional PTO \uD83C\uDFDD️

Remote work from anywhere \uD83D\uDCBB

Economic support for internet and cell phone line\uD83D\uDCF1\uD83C\uDF10

Multidisciplinary, diverse and dynamic team \uD83E\uDDE1

Growth and career path \uD83D\uDE80

Be part of a dynamic team that's creating the next generation payments platform.

The Wireless Software team builds the cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth software that keeps the vehicles online for over-the-air updates, emergency calling, remote commands, navigation, and streaming. We're hiring a senior cellular software engineer to own key parts of the in-vehicle 5G stack on the telematics platform used across several vehicle brands and shipped to markets worldwide. **About Hellyeah AI**  
Hellyeah is the agentic operating system for distribution. AI agents plan, execute and optimize growth work, and humans approve it. A small engineering team runs several live products, with coding agents as part of how we ship.

**The role**  
You will own the platform our products and agents run on: the gateway every model call passes through, the runtime for our production agents, and the clusters, data stores, pipelines, secrets and release paths underneath.

We're hiring two engineers, one in San Francisco and one in Shanghai. One will lean toward the AI platform and the other toward the core platform. You'll share ownership and on-call, and work closely with our CTO.

We run production AI across text, speech and video, mostly through third-party model APIs, with some self-hosted serving. The gateway supports internal teams, our products and customers. We do not train models. If you only want to work on model training, look elsewhere. If you want to make a multi-provider AI stack reliable, secure and affordable, keep reading.

Product teams own product features. IT support, marketing sites and SEO sit outside this role.

**What you'll do**

*The AI platform*

* **Run the model gateway.** Own routing, fallbacks, provider failover, rate limits and rollouts for 90+ model deployments across OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Google and AWS Bedrock. Benchmark new providers on latency, quality, cost and failure behavior before they take traffic, and escalate to vendors when they fall short.
* **Make the gateway multi-tenant.** Give each team and customer the right keys, routes, limits and usage metering, and reconcile usage against provider invoices.
* **Run the AI developer platform.** Own shared coding-agent access, including seats, quotas and per-user limits, plus the remote workspaces our engineers use. One heavy user should never slow down everyone else.
* **Run production agents safely.** Own sandboxing, credential scoping and pinned releases for long-running agents on Kubernetes.
* **Automate your own job.** Expect to build a lot of autonomous infra workflows and infra agents that take on routine requests and alerts, with a person approving risky actions.
* **Own infrastructure and AI spend.** Reconcile provider bills against usage, tie spend to a team and product, and catch anomalies early. Right-size clusters, spend vendor credits before they expire, and handle quota and billing escalations with cloud and model vendors.

*The core platform*

* **Keep clusters and cloud healthy.** Debug and upgrade EKS, AKS and bare-metal k3s through Argo CD and Kustomize. Manage AWS, Azure and GCP through reviewed Terraform.
* **Run the edge.** Own Cloudflare across a dozen domains: DNS, WAF, TLS, CDN and object storage, plus GeoDNS, load balancers, egress IPs and email authentication.
* **Ship new services fast.** Point a coding agent at an open-source repo and have it in production the same day: manifests or Helm, pinned images, Postgres and Redis, SSO, DNS, TLS, secrets and backups, all through GitOps. Make it highly available when it needs to be, and give each service a named owner. Build production infrastructure for new product launches the same way.
* **Hack your way to a solution.** When something blocks you, read the source, patch it, work around it or build what's missing. You always have one more way to solve the problem.
* **Lead migrations.** Move workloads between regions, clouds and platforms with a tested rollback, retire what's left behind, and bring stray services under GitOps.
* **Operate the data layer.** Upgrade and migrate production PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse and Redis, run schema changes safely, and prove backups by restoring them.
* **Keep data pipelines flowing.** Run Airbyte, Airflow, Dataform and CDC into BigQuery so product and finance data stay fresh, and catch a stalled sync before it fills a production disk.

*Reliability and security*

* **Own reliability.** Set SLOs and alerts people trust, lead incidents across infrastructure and product services, including realtime speech, write the reviews, and automate the triage you keep repeating.
* **Own observability.** Keep metrics, logs and traces flowing and usable across every cluster and the gateway. Maintain Grafana, Prometheus, Loki and Datadog, build on OpenTelemetry, add telemetry to new services, and manage retention and cost, so engineers and agents can see what's happening without asking you.
* **Own infrastructure security.** Rotate credentials, replace static keys with workload identity, find exposed secrets and vulnerable dependencies, respond to exposures, and control access to customer data.
* **Make access self-serve.** Replace manual grants with SSO, workload identity and scoped secrets, so engineers get what they need without asking you. Own the OAuth clients and API apps we run on ad and commerce platforms, including their reviews.

*The team around you*

* **Give product teams a paved road.** Build the release pipelines, canaries, preview environments and guardrails that let them ship and operate their own services.
* **Review and teach.** Review infrastructure changes from engineers, founders and their agents, and share the runbooks and agent skills that keep everyone fast.

**Your first 90 days**

* Join on-call and run an incident review.
* Take a new model from benchmark to production traffic.
* Reconcile one month of gateway usage against provider invoices.
* Cut manual access requests in half.
* Put one recurring request or alert under agent handling, with a person approving risky actions.
* Make sure a second person can run each critical system.

**What you'll bring**

* 5+ years running production infrastructure, with real on-call experience
* Deep Kubernetes debugging, including stateful workloads
* Hands-on experience running Kubernetes on bare metal, including storage, networking, upgrades and node failure
* GitOps and Terraform in production, ideally across more than one

**The role**  
You will own the platform our products and agents run on: the gateway every model call passes through, the runtime for our production agents, and the clusters, data stores, pipelines, secrets and release paths underneath.

We're hiring two engineers, one in San Francisco and one in Shanghai. One will lean toward the AI platform and the other toward the core platform. You'll share ownership and on-call, and work closely with our CTO.

Benchmark new providers on latency, quality, cost and failure behavior before they take traffic, and escalate to vendors when they fall short.

The New York Public Library is seeking a Software Engineer III to join our Digital Asset Preservation and Access (DAPA) team, where they will have a major impact on NYPL’s ability to make more of its extensive collections available online. This includes assets available on NYPL’s Digital Collections site, as well other discovery platforms, staff management tools and the systems that support them.

This will involve major contributions to an ongoing initiative to modernize the systems that provide access to these collections, and from there continue to expand them in collaboration with our partners in NYPL’s Research libraries. This strategic work will underlie much of NYPL’s objectives in this area, and is an exciting opportunity for an engineer to identify improvements that will impact all of our patrons.
